## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pabbatūpattharajātaka* (Ja 195) is a story in the canonical Pali *Jātaka* collection. According to the narrative framework preserved in the commentary edited by V. Fausböll, the Buddha delivered this teaching while residing at Jetavana concerning the King of Kosala [Fausböll 1879]. The occasion arose when a minister in the king's service had committed an offense within the royal harem (*antepura*); upon ascertaining the truth of the matter, the king approached Jetavana to consult the Buddha on the appropriate course of action [Fausböll 1879]. The opening verse cited in the commentary begins with the words *Pabbatūpatthare ramme* [Fausböll 1879].
